question: Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f(x)=5-x$. Show that $f$ is its own inverse.
explanation:
Composition of the function with itself
$$(f\circ f)(x)=f(5-x)=5-(5-x)=x.$$

Identity function
Thus,
$$f\circ f=I_{\mathbb{R}}.$$

Inverse relation
A function that gives the identity function when composed with itself is its own inverse.

Conclusion
Therefore,
$$f^{-1}=f$$
and hence
$$f^{-1}(x)=5-x.$$

options.C: $f^{-1}(x)=\frac{1}{5-x}$ because the inverse is the reciprocal
options.D: $f$ has no inverse because it is a decreasing function
